text: Right where we left off: Kanghan's heir doesn't care how brave his husk is.
Moon Ahin, twenty-two: an A-rank summoner called the Puppeteer, and heir to Kanghan's guild. She stands over the abyss like she owns it.
Jaeha's visor fogs up from the inside. Luckily, nobody can see his face.
From the top of a pipe, Nib gives him a flat stare.
She's here to see what her family's cash buys. The foreman can't bow low enough.
She walks past the crew without a glance. To her, their lives come cheaper than her husks.
Jaeha can't resist. He compliments her husks the way he always praised his own.
Moon Ahin doesn't laugh. Ho does, and Woo elbows him.
A flick of the baton, and forty husks fall in behind number four. She wants a guide, not a comedian.
Down they go: Jaeha in front, then Moon Ahin, her forty husks, and the crew.
She's noticed the pencil. A number taking notes is new to her.
So she tests him: how many of hers? He knows, and adds something she didn't ask for.
Two rows of feet hit the steel at the same instant. Perfect drill, and one trap could take the lot.
Then a shriek like tearing metal echoes across the canyon.
A dozen canyon wyverns pour out of the far wall and dive, beaks full of needle teeth.
One flick, and forty husks lock into a shield wall, shoving the crew behind them.
White fists punch the wyverns out of the air, three at a time.
Moon Ahin conducts with small, quick strokes, her face perfectly calm.
But the wall marches onto old stone, right over a live plate. Jaeha shouts, and she hushes him without turning.
The ledge drops away, and three husks fall into the abyss, still in perfect formation.
Her face stays composed. One eyebrow twitches.
Through the gap, a wyvern snatches Ho and hauls him out over the drop. Woo grabs for his boot and misses.
Jaeha decides in a heartbeat. His cover is worth a lot. It isn't worth Ho.
Nib launches off the pipe in field form, amber blazing. The five-minute clock starts.
One stroke, and the wyvern bursts into ash. Ho drops back into Woo's arms.
The rest of the flock wheels round for another pass.
Jaeha explains the stones. Why obey a number? He nods at the gap her husks fell through.
She hates that he's right, and asks him to repeat it anyway.
His plan: safe stones only, and one live stone turned into a trap for the flock.
The husks cross single file. Jaeha calls the steps, and the Puppeteer conducts to someone else's count.
A tail barb rakes Nib's shoulder, and the gash opens on Jaeha's. He keeps calling.
Then his plain husk steps onto the marked stone, the whole flock dives, and stone spikes punch out of the wall through every one.
Ash drifts down like snow. The last two wyverns flee.
Ho lies on his back, laughing like a madman. The chicken shop survives.
Jaeha drops Nib back to rest form early, before anyone looks too closely.
Too late. Moon Ahin walks right up to the masked shape on the rail. She has seen that speed before, on a clip.
Then she flips Jaeha's respirator off with the tip of her baton.
She knows that face. Two million people do. Jaeha tries a weak, polite smile.
Four visors swing his way. The crew finally know who's been walking in front of them. Ho wants him on the shop sign.
The foreman storms up, baton out. Moon Ahin claims the masked husk as her own without blinking, and sends him packing.
Her cover comes with a price: an explanation. Jaeha's honest answer: they came for the same thing.
She holds still a beat. For now, that answer will do.
Down they go, the crew close behind Jaeha now, a faint violet glow inside the pipes.
Pyo limps beside him, a little ashamed. He walked past these pipes without a single question. Jaeha came with plenty.
Pyo's hand on the rail trembles with a deep, slow vibration.
Down at the river, Lyra wrings out her braid and rules the woman in white too pretty to like. Borro knows the pattern.
The wall here is carved: a giant in coral armour holding back a wave with a trident, sea-people kneeling below.
Nib knows that style from home. Those carvers belonged to the coast. So what is their hero doing down here?
At the next landing, a padlocked gate guards a narrow cleft, violet light pulsing deep inside.
The foreman spreads his arms across it: below here is Director Baek's. Moon Ahin reminds him who is inspecting whom, and orders it opened.
She takes one step closer and says it again, very quietly.
His shaking hand unlocks the padlock.
Jaeha and Moon Ahin step into the cleft first, side by side.
Then everything shakes. Dust falls, and forty polished heads tilt up together.
A huge pulse of violet light rolls up from below, the pipes swell like veins, and far down, something vast rises and falls.
Moon Ahin's grip tightens on her baton. Jaeha pulls his respirator off to listen.
At the canyon floor, through Borro's eyes, the river ripples in perfect rings with every beat.
Jaeha counts the beats, because counting is what he does. No pump keeps that rhythm.
Far below, the light pulses again. In three hundred raids, Jaeha has never heard a heartbeat this size.
